LakeShark

FIELD SETUP

A handheld scanner built on an ESP32-P4 and an RTL-SDR dongle. It decodes P25 Phase 1, ADS-B, POCSAG and FM, and a Flipper Zero can drive it over Bluetooth as a second screen.

ARADIO
What you need
BoardWaveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-4.3 (480×800 panel, 32 MB flash)
ReceiverAny RTL-SDR (RTL2832U) dongle. R820T2 or R828D tuner.
AntennaWhatever suits the band. The stock whip is enough to see aircraft.
CablesUSB-C to the board's UART port for flashing. The dongle goes in the USB-A host port.
Only this board is covered here. The Nano, the LCD-4B and the T-Display-P4 build from source but are not packaged.
Install
Needs Chrome, Edge, Brave or Opera on a desktop. Firefox, Safari and phones cannot flash.

Plug the board into your computer by its UART USB-C port, then:

Your browser cannot flash. Use Chrome or Edge on a desktop. Flashing needs a secure connection.

The board appears as a CH343 serial port. If nothing is listed, you are probably in the USB-C port that is wired for USB host rather than UART.

First install writes all four images — bootloader, partition table, application and storage. Do not flash the application alone onto a blank board: the storage partition is mounted without a format-on-failure fallback, so an unwritten one halts the boot.
Do it from a terminal instead

With esptool installed, from the unpacked firmware bundle:

esptool --chip esp32p4 --baud 921600 write_flash \
  --flash_mode dio --flash_freq 80m --flash_size 32MB \
  0x2000    bootloader.bin \
  0x8000    partition-table.bin \
  0x10000   lakeshark.bin \
  0xe10000  storage.bin

Checksums are in SHA256SUMS. Later application-only updates are just the 0x10000 line.

BHEAD

Optional. A Flipper Zero works as a remote screen and keypad over Bluetooth — useful when the radio is in a bag and you are not. Everything below is skippable; the touchscreen does all of it too.

Install
  1. Copy lakeshark_p25.fap to /ext/apps/GPIO/ on the Flipper's SD card.
  2. Turn Bluetooth on in the Flipper's own Settings → Bluetooth. The app cannot turn it on for you.
  3. Open GPIO → LakeShark SDR.
  4. Inside the app: Settings → Link → Transport, set it to Bluetooth.

The radio finds the head on its own from there. It takes a few seconds and the app's status line goes advertising → connected → linked.

The app has to stay open. It owns the Flipper's radio only while it is running. Close it and the Flipper falls back to its normal Bluetooth profile, which is not the one LakeShark looks for.
Bluetooth is remembered only after it has worked once. If a session fails the app returns to the wired UART transport and stays there, so a head that used to connect and now says NO SDR is usually just back on UART — check Settings → Link → Transport before anything else.
Wired instead of Bluetooth

Set Transport to UART and wire radio TX to Flipper RX, radio RX to Flipper TX, common GND. Do not feed the board from Flipper 5 V while it is also on USB.

CUSING IT
First run
  1. Dongle into the USB-A host port, antenna on, power up.
  2. HOME shows the app tiles. Start with ADS-B. It needs no licence, no frequency to guess and no local system to exist — if aircraft appear, the whole chain works.
  3. Then try FM on a broadcast station you know is there. Voice out of the speaker proves the audio path.
  4. P25 last. It only decodes if a P25 Phase 1 system is actually on the air near you, so it is the worst thing to test with first.
Aircraft on ADS-B within a minute or two is the sign everything is healthy: USB host, dongle, tuning, DSP and display.
Getting files off it

Settings → Wi-Fi → SCAN, join your network, and the board serves its SD card at http://<its-address>/. Screenshots and recordings land there. Pulling the shade down from the top of the screen shows the address and has a screenshot button.

When something is wrong
Flipper says NO SDR
Almost always the head, not the radio. Is the app still open? Is Bluetooth on? Is Transport set to Bluetooth? See panel B.
No aircraft on ADS-B
Give it two minutes — it needs an aircraft to transmit. Check the antenna is on the dongle and the dongle is in the USB-A host port, not the UART port.
"Low memory. Tap an app to retry."
Internal RAM ran out while loading. Go back to HOME and open the app again. If it repeats, power-cycle.
An app opens but nothing is received
Power-cycle. A receiver that draws its screen but never tunes has failed to claim the dongle, and a clean boot clears it.
P25 shows activity but no speech
Control-channel traffic is not voice. Valid NACs and TSBKs only mean you found the system; voice needs a talkgroup actually in use, and unencrypted.
Source, issues and the other board targets: github.com/SAMS0N1TE/LakeShark. GPLv3. Receiving is not the same as being allowed to receive — what you may listen to is local law, and yours to check.
